title: Women’s agency is context-specific and cannot safely be measured by one universal survey scale or current generative AI
source_unit: World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11464, Developing a Measure of Women's Agency in Tunisia: Machine Learning and Generative Artificial Intelligence Approaches
geography: Tunisia; qualitative in-depth interviews and quantitative surveys with the same sample of women, including rural and urban context comparisons, with comparison to an India-developed agency measure

observations.period: 2026 paper; Tunisia measure development and India comparison

denominator.unit: women in the Tunisia mixed-methods agency measurement sample

concept.value: agency is defined as the ability to define and act on one's goals

cross_context_overlap.value: overlap between questions performing well in India and Tunisia is minimal

within_country_variation.value: questions selected in one context, such as rural Tunisia, do not necessarily perform well in another, such as urban Tunisia

implication.value: researchers may need context-specific agency measures to measure agency accurately

observations.method: Mixed-methods measure development using qualitative interviews and quantitative surveys from the same women, with machine-learning selection and comparison to a prior India measure.
observations.uncertainty: The findings concern instrument performance and construct measurement in the studied contexts; they do not imply that agency itself is incomparable or that no cross-context core can ever be identified.
observations.subgroup: Women in Tunisia across rural and urban contexts, women in India used for comparison, researchers, program evaluators, and institutions using agency measures to allocate resources.
observations.counterinterpretation: Minimal item overlap may reflect survey wording, translation, sampling, model specification, or benchmark choices as well as genuine contextual differences in how agency is expressed.

observations.period: 2026 paper; machine-learning and generative-AI measure construction

machine_learning.value: machine-learning approaches perform well against a benchmark qualitative agency score

generative_ai.value: generative-AI approaches do not perform comparably against the qualitative benchmark

efficiency_claim.value: current readily available generative-AI tools did not make the exercise more effective or less time-consuming

governance_implication.value: automating question generation or scoring does not remove the need for local qualitative grounding and validation

observations.method: Comparison of machine-learning and generative-AI approaches against a manually coded qualitative agency benchmark, with reproducibility materials documenting data and methods.
observations.uncertainty: Performance depends on the benchmark, prompts, models, training data, language, translation, sample, and validation design; the result is not a universal evaluation of every generative-AI system.
observations.subgroup: Women whose experiences are converted into survey measures, local qualitative researchers, survey designers, AI developers, policymakers, and organizations deploying automated measurement.
observations.counterinterpretation: Future models, better local-language systems, human-AI workflows, or richer prompts may improve performance; current failure does not establish permanent incapacity.

observations.period: 2026 paper; agency measurement and policy interpretation

policy_status.value: agency is both an end in itself and a means of reducing other gender inequities

measurement_risk.value: treating standard large-scale survey measures as universal can obscure local forms of goal definition, action, constraint, and decision-making

institutional_route.value: measurement design affects what programs can see, compare, fund, and evaluate

observations.method: Synthesis of the paper's construct definition, mixed-methods design, context comparisons, and implications for survey and policy measurement.
observations.uncertainty: The record concerns measurement validity and policy interpretation, not a population estimate of women's agency or a causal evaluation of empowerment programs.
observations.subgroup: Women with different household, geographic, cultural, linguistic, economic, and social positions; program implementers and institutions relying on comparable indicators.
observations.counterinterpretation: A universal core can still be useful for broad monitoring if it is supplemented by locally validated modules and interpreted with humility; context-specificity does not require abandoning comparison.

related_sources.claim: Abstract and bibliographic record for World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 11464.
World Bank reproducibility package with sample, data, AI-score, qualitative benchmark, and method metadata.
World Bank MENA Gender Innovation Lab description of the Tunisia agency mixed-methods study.

boundary: This record adds a context-specific agency-measurement route linking qualitative grounding, survey design, machine learning, generative AI, local variation, and policy visibility. It does not provide a universal agency index, population-level agency prevalence, causal empowerment effects, proof that all generative AI fails, or a reason to discard cross-context comparison when locally validated modules are combined with a transparent core.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official World Bank working-paper PDF, abstract, reproducibility package, and MENA Gender Innovation Lab description were reviewed for the 400-woman mixed-methods sample, India-Tunisia overlap, rural-urban variation, machine-learning performance, generative-AI limitation, and policy-measurement boundaries.
